overview: Equatorial Guinea is a small country in Central Africa, made up of a mainland region and several islands. Its capital is Malabo, on the island of Bioko, although a new capital is being built on the mainland. It became independent from Spain in 1968 and is the only country in Africa with Spanish as an official language. Oil has been its main export since the 1990s.

geography.text: The mainland, called Río Muni, lies between Cameroon and Gabon and is covered by rainforest. The island of Bioko, in the Gulf of Guinea, is volcanic and mountainous. The country also includes Annobón, a small island far to the south-west.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Drills (a kind of monkey) and sea turtles on Bioko.

history.text: The island of Bioko was named Fernando Pó after a Portuguese sailor, and Spain took the territory in 1778. It became Spanish Guinea and gained independence in 1968, making it the only African country with Spanish as an official language. Francisco Macías Nguema's rule was brutal; he was overthrown in 1979. Oil was found in the 1990s.

events.text: Fernão do Pó reaches the island.

events.title: Spanish rule
events.text: Portugal hands the territory to Spain.

government.text: Equatorial Guinea is a presidential republic in name, but power is held by President Teodoro Obiang, who has ruled since 1979, making him the world's longest-serving president. His son is Vice President.

economy.text: Oil and gas make up almost all exports. Oil made Equatorial Guinea rich per person on paper, but most people remain poor.

culture.text: Equatorial Guinea is the only African country with Spanish as an official language. It is made up of a mainland region and islands, including Bioko, where the capital Malabo stands.

items.title: Spanish-speaking Africa
items.text: The only Spanish-speaking country in sub-Saharan Africa.

items.title: Bioko
items.text: A volcanic island with rainforest and monkeys.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Independence Day, 12 October, is the main celebration.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Equatorial Guinea co-hosted the Africa Cup of Nations in 2012 and hosted it in 2015, reaching the semi-finals. Swimmer Eric Moussambani became famous at the 2000 Olympics.

items.text: Hosted the Africa Cup of Nations and reached the semi-finals.

items.title: 'Eric the Eel'
items.text: Eric Moussambani had learned to swim just months before the 2000 Olympics.

didYouKnow: Equatorial Guinea's capital, Malabo, is on an island, not the mainland.
It is the only African country with Spanish as an official language.

keyPeople.name: Eric Moussambani
keyPeople.text: Became famous as 'Eric the Eel' at the 2000 Olympics.
